newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh government creates new zinc-lead enterprise.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh government creates new zinc-lead enterprise.

text.p: Kazakhstan is to form one joint-stock company from three troubled enterprises that produce lead and zinc in the northeast of the former Soviet republic, officials said on Wednesday.
A Kazakh government document made available to Reuters said the new company, AO Kaztsink, would be formed from the ageing mines and plants in Ust-Kamenogorsk, Leninogorsk and Zyryanovsk.
The document gave no details on Kaztsink's share structure but said the new enterprise maintained the right to mine the Maleyevsk, Ridder-Sokol and Tishinsk fields.
Officials said the the three plants, which spew tonnes of pollutants on to surrounding towns, have not undergone any modernisation for over a decade.
Combined debts for the three mines and smelting plants total $173 million.
Boris Sadchikov, deputy chief of the metals and mining department at the Kazakh trade and industry ministry, told Reuters the three plants required around $270 million of repairs and modernisation.
"Lead and zinc production this year (1996) will remain around the same as 1995, Sadchikov said.
Lead and zinc production in 1995 totalled 88,500 tonnes and 169,200 tonnes respectively, according to the state statistics committee.
He said production at the three enterprises was stabilising but did not say at what capacity the plants were operating.
In Soviet times, Ust-Kamenogorsk alone produced 100,000 tonnes per year of lead and 180,000 tonnes of zinc.
